payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and extend durability. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit retracted the earlier 12,000-cycle claim, identifying it as an un-normalized measurement; the corrected cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold. Confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At 500 MWh manufacturing scale, projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates below that point, requiring cycling to stop.
